title.value: M ETRO : M EMORY-E NHANCED T RANSFORMER FOR R ETROSYNTHETIC P LANNING VIA R EACTION T REE
title.justification: The title accurately represents the paper's focus on using a memory-enhanced transformer model to improve retrosynthetic planning by leveraging reaction trees.
title.quote: M ETRO : M EMORY-E NHANCED T RANSFORMER FOR R ETROSYNTHETIC P LANNING VIA R EACTION T REE Anonymous authors Paper under double-blind review

extractions.description: The paper presents Metro, a memory-enhanced transformer model for retrosynthetic planning in drug discovery and organic chemistry. This model addresses the limitations of existing single-step retrosynthesis models by capturing the dependency among molecules in a reaction tree for multi-step retrosynthesis predictions. The authors construct a new benchmark consisting of reaction trees and demonstrate that Metro significantly outperforms existing models in accuracy. The proposed model can also be used for synthetic accessibility analysis, offering a novel formulation for retrosynthetic planning tasks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on retrosynthetic planning and improvements in chemical synthesis processes, which are more relevant to organic chemistry and drug discovery rather than direct implications on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Retrosynthetic planning plays a critical role in drug discovery and organic chemistry. Starting from a target molecule as the root node, it aims to find a complete reaction tree subject to the constraint that all leaf nodes belong to a set of starting materials.

primary_category.quote: Retrosynthetic planning is a fundamental problem in organic chemistry... The goal of retrosynthetic planning is to find a series of starting molecules that go through a sequence of reactions, which can also be represented as reaction tree, to synthesize the target molecule.
